name: Dìreach
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Dìreach names one form of the Scottish monster called the fachan, also known as the athach. The fachan stood on one leg and had one eye. It carried a flail covered with iron apples in a hand that grew from its chest. The creature struck at passersby while hopping on that single leg. The dìreach version haunted the lonely Glen Eitive in Scotland. Some writers trace the monster to fear of a druid's cursing posture. A druid cast a curse by standing on one leg with one arm raised in the air. That pose appears in the ritual glám dícenn. The dìreach thus connects a folkloric figure to an old practice rather than to a distinct being.
objective: Define the Dìreach as a form of the Scottish fachan monster and connect it to the druid cursing posture.
key_results: Dìreach is one named form of the Scottish fachan monster.
The fachan had one leg, one eye, and a hand growing from its chest.
The hand held a flail covered with iron apples.
Authors link the monster to a druid's one-legged cursing posture.
evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore (2003): Dìreach; fachan.
